text: BSON Binary subtype 9 is a typed vector envelope: it uses a dtype byte and a padding byte before the packed element data, stores values in little-endian form, and defines FLOAT32 (0x27), INT8 (0x03), and PACKED_BIT (0x10) dtypes. Drivers expose explicit vector encode and decode helpers, such as PyMongo's Binary.from_vector() and Binary.as_vector(). (high confidence)

MongoDB documents about three times less cluster disk space for BinData vectors than standard float32 arrays. Pre-quantized int8 and int1 representations reduce mongot vector RAM by about 3.75x and 24x respectively; the HNSW graph itself does not shrink, so disk and index-memory savings must be estimated separately. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20)

A vector query must use the same embedding model as the indexed data and its length must match numDimensions. A full-fidelity query vector can match BinData(float32) data; using a mismatched subtype with int8 or int1 data can return no results without an error. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

MongoDB Vector Search accepts BSON BinData vector subtypes float32, int8, and int1 in vector index fields. The documented numDimensions range is 1–8192 for int8, a multiple of 8 for int1, and no more than 8192 overall. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

The client must convert pre-quantized embeddings to BSON BinData subtype 9 before inserting them, using a driver that supports vector encoding. The current MongoDB guide lists minimum supported driver versions, and PyMongo added Binary.from_vector() and Binary.as_vector() in version 4.10. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

Quantization can trade retrieval precision for lower memory and faster comparisons. MongoDB's benchmark says binary quantization can materially reduce search precision and that rescoring candidates from full-fidelity vectors adds latency, so resource ratios do not guarantee equal quality or lower end-to-end latency for every embedding model and workload. (medium confidence)

Embedding APIs can return quantized outputs, but those outputs are not automatically BSON vector values. Voyage AI and Cohere document int8 and binary-family output choices, while BSON subtype 9 requires its own dtype and padding metadata; convert the provider output using a compatible driver and verify the exact binary representation. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20)

PyMongo 4.10 introduced provisional subtype 9 support, and PyMongo 4.10.1 fixed a subtype 9 bug on big-endian systems. Early PyMongo 4.10.0 deployments on big-endian hosts therefore needed the 4.10.1 fix for portable vector serialization. (high confidence)

MongoDB Vector Search supports pre-quantized BinData vectors with float32, int8, or int1 types. The documented maximum dimensionality is 8192 for int8, while int1 dimensions must be a multiple of 8; int1 supports euclidean similarity, and int8 supports cosine, euclidean, or dotProduct. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

The current MongoDB guide lists driver minimums for BinData vector ingestion: C++ 4.1.0, C#/.NET 3.2.0, Go 2.1.0, PyMongo 4.10, Node.js 6.11, Java 5.3.1, and Ruby bson gem 5.1. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

The PyMongo Binary API provides from_vector(vector, dtype, padding=0), and the Node.js BSON Binary API provides fromFloat32Array, fromInt8Array, and fromPackedBits constructors for subtype-9 vectors. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20)

Voyage AI and Cohere embedding APIs expose selectable output formats that include float and quantized integer or packed-binary forms, with supported formats depending on the model. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20)

Do not write provider binary or ubinary output bytes as a subtype-9 value without conversion: subtype 9 requires dtype and padding metadata before the packed elements. Validate the provider's bit order and padding against PACKED_BIT requirements before ingestion. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20)

MongoDB documentation estimates that BinData vectors use about three times less disk space than standard float32 arrays; the vector-search HNSW graph remains separate and is not compressed by vector quantization. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)
